notes: SHIP v1.14.380 - THE RIP-CORD GETS A WAY BACK. Owner: fix the rip-cord, option A. Item 2 of the three-way split from the AUDIT-LEGACY-PARAM audit; item 1 was .379 (glowtune removed) and item 3, legacy removal proper as the R1 pass, is still not started. THE DEFECT: ?legacy=1 is STICKY BY DESIGN - redesign_isOn() writes phantom_legacy='1' into localStorage the moment it sees the param, so every later bare-URL load stays legacy. That persistence is intentional and correct for a field fallback. What was missing is the way back: redesign_initToggle() early-returns when legacy is on, so NOTHING in the legacy house could clear the pin, and the only escape was knowing to type ?redesign=1. A laptop was stranded in legacy mid-verify because of exactly this, and because #ref-grid is display:none outside body.rd, that laptop was showing none of the .378 cards while appearing to work - a silent invalidation of a device check. A rip-cord you cannot climb back up is a trap, not a rip-cord. THE FIX, one function and one menu item. legacy_returnToNewUI() clears phantom_legacy and navigates to ?redesign=1 rather than doing a bare reload, so the un-stick still works even when removeItem throws - private mode, disabled storage, quota. Per the No Silent Failures rule the catch warns to console AND raises a phantomToast rather than swallowing, and the navigation happens either way. The control is one button appended as the last entry of the legacy SYS overflow menu (#hdr-overflow-menu), alongside Export, Import, Identity, Action Stripe, HW REF and Site Profile - a menu entry, not chrome, which is the smallest visible change that actually solves it. RULE 7 - THIS IS THE PART THAT NEEDED AN OWNER RULING AND GOT ONE. CLAUDE.md rule 7 makes legacy markup untouchable outside a John-signed pass, and every genuine fix here touches legacy, because being stranded in legacy is the whole problem. That conflict was put to the owner rather than absorbed, and option A - the menu item - was chosen over option B, which would have made the pin non-persistent or self-expiring. B was rejected as the worse failure: it needs no markup change but would yank a tech who deliberately chose the fallback back into the redesign, possibly mid-shift. CONTAINMENT, verified rather than asserted: the new button sits inside #hdr-overflow-wrap, which line 9630 hides with display:none !important under body.rd. Confirmed by line arithmetic - the wrap opens at 12963 and the button is at 12982 - so the redesign house cannot render it, and this ship changes the legacy house only, deliberately and with sign-off. NOT TOUCHED: redesign_isOn() itself and its 106 call sites, the 441 body.rd-scoped rules, the persistence semantics of the flag, the legacy nav, #ops-tab-strip, sw.js beyond its cache stamp, and all art from .377/.378. DEVICE-VERIFY, and this one is best done on the laptop that is currently stuck: (1) badge reads v1.14.380 - you may need ?redesign=1 once to see it, which is the very thing this ship removes the need for. (2) Load ?legacy=1 deliberately. (3) Open the SYS overflow menu in the legacy header - RETURN TO NEW UI should be the last item, teal. (4) Tap it: the app should reload into the redesign and STAY there on subsequent bare-URL loads. That is the whole ship. (5) Confirm the item is ABSENT from the redesign house - open the same overflow affordance under the new UI and it must not appear at all. (6) Legacy rendering otherwise unchanged - same header, same nav, same pages. (7) ?legacy=1 still pins as before; persistence was deliberately kept. ROLLBACK: revert this commit - removes the handler and the menu item together and restores the previous stamps.
